doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Buddy Rich, Alvino Rey and Manhattan School
title: The Jimmy Dorsey trombone book and Bobby Byrne
summary: Mandel describes the trombone chair in Jimmy Dorsey's band, written for Tommy-style players, and following Bobby Byrne and Moe Zudekoff.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: One of your successors with Jimmy Dorsey, Bobby Byrne.
He was there well before me.
Apparently he took over when Tommy left.
That’s right, he did and he was a good trombone player, but he was kind of, sort of like Tommy in that way, you know he was a very good smooth trombone player. Very good musician.
And reputedly a better jazz player than Tommy.
I didn’t know – yeah, he wasn’t a great jazz player, he had a real good sound though. That was a hard trombone book I’ll tell ya, because it was always written for guys who played like Tommy.
So you were up in the stratosphere a good deal of the time.
That’s why I could cut it.
I took Buddy Morrow’s place, Moe Zudekoff.
Oh. One of the world’s loudest trombone players.
I mean those guys, if I had known what I was doing I would never have followed them.
